raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
_(the text below is written by myself)_

Purpose
1. increase standardization without imposing restrictions on kernel implementations
2. limit LoC changes in model files as a result from adding numerous specialized decode kernels

The kernels themselves will naturally remain difficult to review thoroughly, but **ideally model code should remain easy to review**. The abstraction layer should deliberately be made as thin as possible,

**Note: you can run with either `--monokernel` or `--specialized-decode monokernel`**

# Claims

1. Add `DecodeSpec` and `SpecializedDecode` abstractions in `vllm/models/common/specialized_decode/` 
2. Refactor DSv41 on gfx950 and gfx942 to use these abstractions
3. No regression

For details on point 1, see design doc in the end of the PR description.

# Validation 

Check no regression on dsv41

# 1. DeepSeek-v41 on MI350

On MI350, force max 8 seqs
```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --speculative-config "{\"method\":\"dspark\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":5}" \
  [--specialized-decode]
```

## 1. Performance non-regression check

```
vllm bench serve \
  --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 65536 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --max-concurrency "$CONC" --num-prompts "$((CONC*10))" --num-warmups "$((CONC*2))" \
  --ignore-eos --seed 0 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

Hi @simondanielsson  thanks for the work! For now I have one concern over the `specialized_decode` everywhere stlye abstraction. mono kernel is only a subset of "specialized decode" which is dedicated to small batch size inference. using `--specialized-decode` to enable mono kernel feature would be a blocker and leads to confusions in the future if we add  more specialized decoding method. I would recomment 1. still keep `--monokernel` as a valid option as it's straightforward, and keep our recipes remain coorect, 2. make the flag as an config choice, e.g. `--specialized-decode monokernel` for future compatability.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The layout every MonoKernel's error words and fault hook follow.
+
+A rank's health words: a header whose word FAILED is set once any of its
+in-kernel waits gave up (sticky: a failed rank stays failed, and its later waits
+exit at once), then one record a CTA of the first wait it gave up on (flag,
+region id, pair index, tag, seen tag, CTA, clock, pad).
+
+The output rank's flags: one int32 word a TP rank in the first PEER_HEAD bytes
+of the output rank's peer buffer. A rank whose wait gives up writes its word
+there, drains the store, then sets FAILED, so nothing it stores later can
+overtake the flag. The runner reads these words after every step.
+"""
+
+MONO_ABI_VERSION = 1
+
+RECORD_WORDS = 8
+FAILED = 0
+PEER_HEAD = 256

+        kw: dict[str, Any] = {}
+        if self.index:
+            kw["select"] = lambda normed, qr: _select(layer, positions, normed, qr)
+        if self.ratio:
+            comp = md[cast("str", self.comp_key)]
+            kw.update(
+                topk_indices=attn.topk_indices_buffer,
+                comp_cache=_record_view(
+                    attn._compressed_kv_cache(), comp.block_size // self.ratio
+                ),
+                comp_block_table=comp.block_table,
+            )
+        return runner.forward(
+            self.weights,
+            x,
+            residual,
+            post_mix,
+            res_mix,
+            pre_mix,
+            positions,
+            swa.slot_mapping,
+            _record_view(attn.swa_cache_layer.kv_cache, swa.block_size),
+            swa.decode_swa_indices,
+            swa.decode_swa_lens,
+            swa.token_to_req_indices,
+            fold=fold,
+            **kw,
+        )
+
+
+class FfnSeam(DSV41LayerKernel):
+    """The FFN seam, MoE and both reductions as one launch, from wo_b's
+    unreduced output after vLLM's attention."""
+
+    ffn_only = True
+
+    def warmup_keys(self) -> list[Any]:
+        return [(self.width, "ffn")]
+
+    def compile(self, key: Any) -> None:
+        self.launch_state.runner.scratch(key[0])
+        self.launch_state.runner.ffn_kernel(key[0])
+
+    def launch(
+        self,
+        part: torch.Tensor,
+        residual: torch.Tensor,
+        post_mix: torch.Tensor,
+        res_mix: torch.Tensor,
+        pre_mix: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...] | None:
+        tensors = (part, residual, post_mix, res_mix, pre_mix)
+        if not all(t.is_contiguous() for t in tensors):
+            return None
+        return self.launch_state.runner.ffn(self.weights, *tensors)
+
+
+def _compute_units() -> int:
+    return current_platform.num_compute_units(torch.accelerator.current_device_index())
+
+
+def _widths(vllm_config) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+    """The configured capture sizes the kernels can serve, so a deployment
+    that asked for fewer graphs keeps them; every size at all when it asked for
+    none."""
+    sizes = vllm_config.compilation_config.cudagraph_capture_sizes or []
+    served = tuple(s for s in sorted(sizes) if 1 <= s <= MAX_ROWS)
+    return served or tuple(range(1, MAX_ROWS + 1))
+
+
+def _refuse_config(vllm_config) -> list[str]:
+    """Every reason this config cannot run the kernels, before load."""
+    reasons = []
+    if vllm_config.parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size not in (2, 4):
+        reasons.append("needs tensor parallel size 2 or 4")
+    if envs.VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4:
+        reasons.append(
+            "needs AITER's A8W4 MoE (VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4 unset)"
+        )
+    try:
+        import vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.runner  # noqa: F401
+    except ImportError as err:
+        reasons.append(f"needs FlyDSL and AITER's FlyDSL helpers ({err})")
+    return reasons
+
+
+def _refuse_model(model) -> list[str]:
+    """Every reason the loaded model and this GPU cannot run the kernels. The
+    kernels read every one of the 384 experts on each rank, TP-sharded, in
+    AITER's A8W4 MXFP4 layout, from CTAs that all stay resident."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.oracle.mxfp4 import Mxfp4MoeBackend
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.runner import BLOCKS
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import get_cdna_version
+
+    reasons = []
+    if get_cdna_version() not in CDNA_VERSIONS:
+        reasons.append(f"needs CDNA{'/'.join(map(str, CDNA_VERSIONS))}")
+    cus = _compute_units()
+    if cus < BLOCKS:
+        reasons.append(f"needs {BLOCKS} compute units, the GPU has {cus}")
+    backends = set()
+    for layer in model.layers:
+        experts = getattr(getattr(layer, "ffn", None), "experts", None)
+        routed = getattr(experts, "routed_experts", None)
+        if routed is not None:
+            backends.add(getattr(routed.quant_method, "mxfp4_backend", None))
+    wrong = backends - {Mxfp4MoeBackend.AITER_MXFP4_BF16}
+    if wrong:
+        reasons.append(f"needs the AITER_MXFP4_BF16 MoE backend, not {wrong}")
+    return reasons
+
+
+def _skip_layer(layer) -> str | None:
+    """Why this layer keeps vLLM's path for every step, or None when it takes a
+    launch (whole or FFN only: ``_build`` picks which)."""
+    ffn = layer.ffn
+    if layer.use_sequence_parallel:
+        return "sequence-parallel layer"
+    if not layer.fuse_seam_norm:
+        return "needs aiter's fused mHC seam"
+    if (
+        ffn.shared_experts is None
+        or ffn.gate.tid2eid is not None
+        or ffn.n_routed_experts != 384
+        or ffn.n_activated_experts != 6
+        or ffn.routed_scaling_factor != 1.5
+        or ffn.swiglu_limit != 10.0
+        or ffn.scoring_func != "sqrtsoftplus"
+        or not ffn.renormalize
+    ):
+        return "MoE routing outside the kernels' (384 / 6, sqrtsoftplus, x1.5)"
+    return None
+
+
+def _ffn_only(layer) -> str | None:
+    """Why this layer's attention seam and attention stay on vLLM's path, which
+    leaves it the FFN launch, or None when it runs whole."""
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.rocm import DeepseekV41RocmMxfp4Indexer
+
+    attn = layer.attn
+    if attn.compressor is not None and attn.indexer is None:
+        return "a compressor without an indexer"
+    if attn.indexer is not None and not isinstance(
+        attn.indexer, DeepseekV41RocmMxfp4Indexer
+    ):
+        return f"a {type(attn.indexer).__name__}"
+    if attn.compress_ratio not in (0, 1, 2):
+        return f"compress ratio {attn.compress_ratio}"
+    if attn.kv_mxfp8 or attn.kv_cache_dtype != "fp8_ds_mla":
+        return f"a {attn.kv_cache_dtype} KV cache"
+    return None
+
+
+def _skip_step(vllm_config, launch_state: LaunchState, width: int) -> str | None:
+    """Why this step keeps vLLM's path at every layer, or None when the kernels
+    take it. One verdict for every kernel layer, from the batch the whole TP
+    group sees alike."""

+    md = fc.attn_metadata

+def _record_view(kv: torch.Tensor, block: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """A layer's fp8_ds_mla cache as [blocks, block, RECORD] bytes (a block's
+    data rows, then its scale words: the kernels index both from it)."""
+    kv = kv if kv.dtype == torch.uint8 else kv.view(torch.uint8)
+    return torch.as_strided(kv, (kv.shape[0], block, RECORD), (kv.stride(0), RECORD, 1))
+
+
+def _scale_bytes(scale: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return scale if scale.dtype == torch.uint8 else scale.view(torch.uint8)
+

+def _select(
+    layer: "DeepseekV4DecoderLayer",
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    normed: torch.Tensor,
+    qr: torch.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    """An index source's compressor and top-k selection, from K1's normed input
+    and bf16 qr: ``_forward_csa2_full`` / ``_forward_csa2_reindex`` and the
+    indexer op, serial."""
+    attn = layer.attn
+    comp, indexer = attn.compressor, attn.indexer
+    assert indexer is not None
+    if comp is not None:
+        kv_score = torch.mm(
+            normed, comp.fused_wkv_wgate.weight.T, out_dtype=torch.float32
+        )
+        latent = comp(kv_score, positions)
+        comp.insert_cache(latent, positions, attn.rotary_emb)
+        indexer._produce_k(latent, positions, attn.indexer_rotary_emb)
+    weights, _ = indexer.weights_proj(normed)
+    q, q_scale, weights = indexer.forward_q(
+        qr, None, weights, positions, attn.indexer_rotary_emb
+    )
+    assert weights is not None
+    indexer.indexer_op(
+        normed, (q, q_scale) if q_scale is not None else q, None, weights
+    )

One check needs to come back. `_record_view` treats the KV cache as `[blocks, block, RECORD]` and steps to the next block with `kv.stride(0)`. That stride has to be at least `block * RECORD`, or the next block starts inside the current one. `refuse_caches` only checks `stride(0) < RECORD`. Please validate `kv.stride(0) >= block * RECORD` before creating the view.

On MI350 the monokernel ITL matches main. The tok/s gaps follow acceptance on a short random bench. GSM8K and GPQA stay within stderr.

_(the text below is written by myself)_

Purpose
1. increase standardization without imposing restrictions on kernel implementations
2. limit LoC changes in model files as a result from adding numerous specialized decode kernels

The kernels themselves will naturally remain difficult to review thoroughly, but **ideally model code should remain easy to review**. The abstraction layer should deliberately be made as thin as possible,

**Note: you can run with either `--monokernel` or `--specialized-decode monokernel`**

# Claims

1. Add `DecodeSpec` and `SpecializedDecode` abstractions in `vllm/models/common/specialized_decode/` 
2. Refactor DSv41 on gfx950 and gfx942 to use these abstractions
3. No regression

For details on point 1, see design doc in the end of the PR description.

# Validation 

Check no regression on dsv41

+# Specialized Decode Kernels
+
+## Motivation
+
+A **specialized decode kernel** replaces part or all of a model's decode step with a single hand-written launch. At the small batch sizes of low-latency serving, the regular path is dominated by launch overhead, so one persistent kernel can be much faster. The monokernel (FlyDSL, AMD) is one. Kimi K3's CuTeDSL executor is another. More are coming.
+
+Each one used to bring its own glue into model files. `vllm/models/common/specialized_decode/` replaces that glue with one contract, so model code remains easy to review as the number of kernels grows.
+
+An author writes the specialized kernel, a `DecodeSpec` saying under what conditions it can run, and a `DecodeImpl` dispatcher to connect the kernel to the model code. The following is then handled by the library:
+
+- JIT warm-up registration
+- the config and model checks
+- per-forward choice between the kernel and vLLM's path
+- TP rank agreement on all of it
+- setting CUDA graph capture sizes
+- and picking between several kernels for one model, for instance based on hardware architecture.
+
+Key design principles:
+
+- **The kernel owns its layer loop**: the library has no opinion about layers, so a kernel may replace one layer, two, or the whole backbone
+- **Default deny**: an feature the spec does not list refuses the deployment at startup
+- **Refusals carry reasons**: every check returns strings, which are logged and raised
+- **Three touch points in the model**: construct, build, forward. Nothing in the decoder layer
+- **No kernel code in the contract**: the library is plain Python and imports no vendor runtime, so it loads on any platform
+
+## Quick Overview
+
+### Declaring a Spec
+
+A spec says when the kernel can run and how to build it. It holds no kernel code, so it is evaluated before anything vendor-specific loads:
+
+```python
+# vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/specialized_decode/spec.py
+from vllm.models.common.specialized_decode.spec import DecodeSpec, Feature
+
+
+def _refuse_config(vllm_config) -> list[str]:
+    reasons = []
+    if vllm_config.parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size not in (2, 4, 8):
+        reasons.append("needs tensor parallel size 2, 4 or 8")
+    return reasons
+
+
+def _build(vllm_config, model, widths):
+    from .runtime.decode import DSV41Kernel  # the kernel import stays lazy
+
+    return DSV41Kernel(vllm_config, model, widths)
+
+
+DECODE_SPEC = DecodeSpec["DSV41Kernel"](
+    name="dsv41-cdna4",
+    supports=frozenset({Feature.PIPELINE_PARALLEL, Feature.SPECULATIVE_DECODING}),
+    widths=lambda cfg: tuple(range(1, 49)),
+    refuse_config=_refuse_config,
+    refuse_model=_refuse_model,
+    refuse_caches=_refuse_caches,
+    skip_step=_skip_step,
+    build=_build,
+)
+```
+
+| Field | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `name` | Log and metric name. |
+| `supports` | Engine features this spec serves. Default deny. |
+| `widths` | The step sizes a launch serves, read from the config. |
+| `refuse_config` | Why the config cannot run it. Checked before load. |
+| `refuse_model` | Why the loaded model cannot run it. Checked after load. |
+| `refuse_caches` | Why the KV caches cannot be read. Checked when they are bound. |
+| `skip_step` | Why *this* step should run vLLM's path instead. |
+| `build` | Builds this rank's kernel. |
+| `pad_steps` | Whether a short step launches at the next width up. Off by default. |
+| `set_capture_sizes` | Whether the widths become the capture sizes. On by default. |
+
+`widths` is a function of the config, so a spec can read the GPU. One kernel may take 48 rows on gfx950 but only 42 on gfx942, where the workgroup has less LDS.
+
+### Implementing the Kernel
+
+The kernel stands in for the entire model forward:
+
+```python
+class DecodeImpl(Protocol):
+    cache_layers: tuple[str, ...]
+
+    def run(self, step: Step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs) -> Any: ...
+    def bind_caches(self, caches: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None: ...
+```
+
+`run` takes and returns exactly what the model's own forward does. `step` carries the row count, the width to launch at, and the positions. There is deliberately no further constraint on how `run` is written: FlyDSL and CuTeDSL kernels are structured very differently, and forcing one shape would cost more than it saves.
+
+A kernel that compiles lazily, from one key per launch, can also implement `DecodeWarmable`:
+
+```python
+@runtime_checkable
+class DecodeWarmable(Protocol):
+    def warmup_keys(self) -> list[Any]: ...
+    def compile(self, key: Any) -> None: ...
+```
+
+The dispatcher then registers it with vLLM's JIT warm-up, so the first decode step does not pay the compile. This is optional. Kimi K3 compiles eagerly while it builds, implements neither method, and hence registration is skipped.
+
+!!! note
+    Warm-up is the one part of the contract with a placement requirement. vLLM's warm-up registry is only active while the model loads, so a kernel that wants automatic warm-up must be built in `process_weights_after_loading`. Building later is fine, it just means warming up eagerly.
+
+### Wiring It Into the Model
+
+Three touch points, all on the causal LM:
+
+```python
+class MyForCausalLM(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config, prefix=""):
+        self.decode_spec = select_decode_spec(vllm_config, SPECS)
+        self.specialized_decode: SpecializedDecode[MyKernel] | None = None
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self):
+        if self.decode_spec is not None:
+            self.specialized_decode = SpecializedDecode(
+                self.model, self.vllm_config, self.decode_spec
+            )
+
+    def forward(self, input_ids, positions, intermediate_tensors=None,
+                inputs_embeds=None, **kwargs):
+        decode = self.specialized_decode
+        if decode is not None:
+            step = decode.plan(positions, intermediate_tensors)
+            if step is not None:
+                return decode.run(step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs)
+        return self.model(input_ids, positions, intermediate_tensors,
+                          inputs_embeds, **kwargs)
+```
+
+Plus one hook, so the kernel sees the KV caches once the runner has bound them:
+
+```python
+class MyModelState(DefaultModelState):
+    def initialize_kv_cache(self, kv_cache_config, block_tables):
+        super().initialize_kv_cache(kv_cache_config, block_tables)
+        if self.model.specialized_decode is not None:
+            self.model.specialized_decode.bind_caches()
+```
+
+Nothing else changes. In particular, the decoder layer does not.
+
+!!! warning
+    The model must not carry `@support_torch_compile`. A specialized decode replaces the layer loop, so a `torch.compile`'d model is refused with a message saying so.
+
+### Enabling It
+
+```bash
+vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1 --specialized-decode monokernel
+vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1 --specialized-decode auto  # vLLM picks
+vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1 --monokernel               # shorthand, will be deprecated
+```
+
+## Lifecycle
+
+```text
+Model.__init__
+    ↓
+[select_decode_spec] → None if the flag is off
+                     → the first spec whose refuse_config() is empty
+                     → raises DecodeUnsupported if none fits
+                     → optionally sets the CUDA graph capture sizes to the widths
+    ↓
+process_weights_after_loading
+    ↓
+[SpecializedDecode(...)] → refuse_model(), then agree across the TP group
+                         → spec.build() → the kernel
+                         → register warmup_keys()/compile() with the JIT warm-up
+    ↓
+ModelState.initialize_kv_cache          (runs twice: profiling cache, then the real one)
+    ↓
+[bind_caches] → refuse_caches(), if ok then kernel.bind_caches()
+    ↓
+forward, every step
+    ↓
+[plan] → None (run vLLM's path) if: unserved width,
+         no forward context, piecewise CUDA graph, caches not bound,
+         or skip_step() gave a reason
+    ↓
+[run] → kernel.run(step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs)
+```
+
+## Core Concepts
+
+### Refuse Versus Skip
+
+**Refuse** means the deployment is wrong. It raises `DecodeUnsupported` and the engine does not start. Use it for anything a request cannot change. Example: the parallelism, the GPU, the quantization backend, the cache layout. A silent fallback here would hide a misconfiguration behind a quiet performance loss.
+
+**Skip** means this one step is not for the kernel. `skip_step` returns a reason, `plan()` returns None, and the model's own forward runs. Use it for anything that varies step to step: a prefill in the batch, an unserved row count, missing metadata.
+
+Every rank must reach the same verdict, or the ranks that took the kernel will wait on collectives the others never issue. The library handles this.
+
+### Features
+
+`supports` is default deny. The library works out which features the config turned on, subtracts the spec's set, and refuses whatever is left, naming it. `Feature` covers the parallelism modes, LoRA, KV connectors, EPLB, sleep mode, CPU weight offload, weight updates, routed expert capture and ubatching.
+
+Two checks are enabled by default.
+
+1. the engine must be on Model Runner V2
+1. the CUDA graph mode is `FULL`
+
+### Widths and Capture Sizes
+
+A kernel is built for a fixed set of row counts, and a step of any other size cannot launch. There are two ways to handle that:
+
+- **Exact (default).** `select_decode_spec` amends the CUDA graph capture sizes to the served widths, keeping any size larger than the widest launch. A step off the list falls back to vLLM's path.
+- **Padded.** With `pad_steps=True` a short step launches at the next width up and the kernel owns the padding. Such a spec usually also sets `set_capture_sizes=False`, so the deployment keeps the capture sizes it asked for. A kernel built at `(1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8)` then serves a batch of 3 on the size-4 launch.
+
+### Cache Binding
+
+`cache_layers` names the attention layers whose KV caches the kernel reads. `bind_caches()` looks each up in the static forward context, runs `spec.refuse_caches`, and only then hands them to the kernel, which therefore never sees a cache its spec has not accepted. The hook fires twice during startup, once for the profiling cache and once for the real one. `plan()` refuses to run before the first call, so a model that forgets the hook falls back to vLLM's path rather than reading unbound memory.
+
+## Recipes
+
+### Two Kernels for One Model
+
+Write the second kernel, then add a second spec and list it in preference order:
+
+```python
+DECODE_SPEC_GFX942 = DecodeSpec["DSV41Gfx942Kernel"](
+    name="dsv41-cdna3",
+    supports=frozenset({Feature.PIPELINE_PARALLEL}),   # no spec decode here
+    widths=lambda cfg: tuple(range(1, 17)),            # fewer rows than gfx950
+    refuse_config=_refuse_config_gfx942,               # "needs a gfx942 GPU"
+    refuse_model=_refuse_model,                        # shared with gfx950
+    refuse_caches=_refuse_caches,
+    skip_step=_skip_step,
+    build=_build_gfx942,
+)
+
+SPECS = (DECODE_SPEC_GFX950, DECODE_SPEC_GFX942)
+```
+
+The model already passes `SPECS` to `select_decode_spec`, so nothing else changes. The dispatcher takes the first spec that accepts the config. Specializing on anything other than the architecture works the same way: a kernel that only handles batch size 1 sets `widths=lambda cfg: (1,)` and goes first in the list.
+
+### A Kernel That Covers Part of a Layer
+
+Sometimes we want to write a specialized kernel for part of a layer. For instance, DeepSeek-V4.1 has layers where only the FFN seam uses a specialized kernel but attention runs in normal vLLM code. The library needs no concept of this, because the kernel owns the layer loop and decides per layer:
+
+```python
+# in DecodeImpl.run:
+for idx in range(self.embed_layer, self.layer_end):
+    layer, plan = model.layers[idx], self.plans.get(...)
+    ffn = out = None
+    if plan.ffn_only:
+        ffn = partial(self.launch_ffn, plan)      # a seam, not a layer
+    else:
+        out = self.launch_whole(plan, hidden, positions, ...)
+    if out is None:
+        # inject the specialized kernel into the vLLM execution path
+        out = layer(hidden, positions, ..., decode_ffn=ffn)
+```
+
+The decoder layer can then decide where to use `decode_ffn`.
+
+### A Kernel on a Speculator's Draft Head
+
+A drafter needs its own spec, and additionally needs to plug into the target model's KV cache binding hook.
+
+The draft's causal LM carries the same three touch points as the target:
+
+```python
+# vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/dspark.py
+class DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config, prefix=""):
+        self.specialized_decode_spec = select_decode_spec(
+            vllm_config, DRAFT_DECODE_SPEC
+        )
+        self.specialized_decode: SpecializedDecode[DSV41DraftKernel] | None = None
+        self.model = DSparkDeepseekV4Model(vllm_config=vllm_config, ...)
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self):
+        if self.specialized_decode_spec is not None and self.specialized_decode is None:
+            self.specialized_decode = SpecializedDecode(
+                self.model, self.vllm_config, self.specialized_decode_spec
+            )
+            # register the specialized drafter
+            _DRAFT_DECODES.append(self.specialized_decode)
+
+    def forward(self, input_ids, positions, inputs_embeds=None):
+        if self.specialized_decode is not None:
+            step = self.specialized_decode.plan(positions)
+            if step is not None:
+                return self.specialized_decode.run(step, input_ids, inputs_embeds)
+        return self.model(input_ids, positions, inputs_embeds)
+```
+
+Since the drafter doesn't have its own `ModelState`, we leverage the target model's model state to bind the drafter's caches. We do this by amending the target's `initialize_kv_cache` to also bind the cache of any registered drafter:
+
+```python
+# vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/dspark.py
+_DRAFT_DECODES: list[SpecializedDecode] = []
+
+
+def bind_draft_decode_caches() -> None:
+    for decode in _DRAFT_DECODES:
+        decode.bind_caches()
+
+
+# vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model_state.py
+class DeepseekV41ROCMModelState(DeepseekV41ModelState):
+    def initialize_kv_cache(self, kv_cache_config, block_tables):
+        super().initialize_kv_cache(kv_cache_config, block_tables)
+        if self.model.specialized_decode is not None:
+            self.model.specialized_decode.bind_caches()
+        # NEW
+        bind_draft_decode_caches()
+```
+
+## See Also
+
+- [CUDA Graphs](cuda_graphs.md), the capture sizes a spec amends
+- [Model Runner V2](model_runner_v2.md), the runner a specialized decode requires

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""What a model's ``DecodeSpec`` must satisfy."""
+
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.config.compilation import CUDAGraphMode
+from vllm.forward_context import ForwardContext, override_forward_context
+from vllm.models.common.specialized_decode.dispatch import SpecializedDecode
+from vllm.models.common.specialized_decode.guards import select_decode_spec
+
+KERNEL_BACKENDS = ("aiter", "flydsl")
+"""Backends a spec module must not pull in of its own: it is imported at config
+time, before anything has decided the spec can run. The package holding it is
+the model's own hardware entry point, which already pulls its platform's
+backend, so only what the spec module adds on top of that package counts."""
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def forward(config, mode: CUDAGraphMode, attn_metadata: Any) -> Iterator[None]:
+    """One forward pass's context, as a runner would set it."""
+    context = ForwardContext(
+        no_compile_layers=config.compilation_config.static_forward_context,
+        attn_metadata=attn_metadata,
+        slot_mapping={},
+        cudagraph_runtime_mode=mode,
+    )
+    with override_forward_context(context):
+        yield
+
+
+class DecodeConformance:
+    """What every model's ``DecodeSpec`` must satisfy. Subclass it in the
+    model's test module and fill in the hooks below."""
+
+    specs: tuple[Any, ...]
+    """The model's variants, as it passes them to ``select_decode_spec``."""
+
+    specs_module: str
+    """Where ``specs`` is defined, for the import test to load on its own."""
+
+    def make_config(self, **overrides) -> Any:
+        """A config this spec serves, with ``overrides`` applied on top."""
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+    def make_model(self, config) -> Any:
+        """A loaded model this spec serves, with its KV caches bound into
+        ``config.compilation_config.static_forward_context``."""
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+    def bad_caches(self, config, model) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Caches that break at least two of ``refuse_caches``'s checks."""
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+    @pytest.fixture
+    def config(self):
+        return self.make_config()
+
+    @pytest.fixture
+    def model(self, config):
+        return self.make_model(config)
+
+    @pytest.fixture
+    def decode(self, config, model):
+        return self.make_decode(config, model)
+
+    def make_decode(self, config, model=None, bind: bool = True):
+        """This rank's ``SpecializedDecode``, built the way a model builds it:
+        the variant picked once by ``select_decode_spec``, then the dispatch
+        over the loaded model, then the caches the runner binds."""
+        model = self.make_model(config) if model is None else model
+        spec = select_decode_spec(config, self.specs)
+        assert spec is not None
+        decode = SpecializedDecode(model, config, spec)
+        if bind:
+            decode.bind_caches()
+        return decode
+
+    def test_spec_module_imports_no_kernel_backend(self):
+        module = self.specs_module
+        package = module.rpartition(".")[0]
+        source = (
+            "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '.'); import importlib;"
+            f"importlib.import_module({package!r});"
+            "loaded = set(sys.modules);"
+            f"importlib.import_module({module!r});"
+            "print('\\n'.join(set(sys.modules) - loaded))"
+        )
+        loaded = subprocess.run(
+            [sys.executable, "-c", source],
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+            check=True,
+        ).stdout.split()
+        pulled = {n.split(".")[0] for n in loaded} & set(KERNEL_BACKENDS)
+        assert not pulled, f"{module} imports {sorted(pulled)}"
+
+    def test_refuse_caches_reports_every_reason(self, config, model, decode):
+        reasons = decode.spec.refuse_caches(
+            decode.vllm_config, decode.kernel, self.bad_caches(config, model)
+        )
+        assert len(reasons) >= 2, reasons
+
+    def test_build_does_not_move_weights(self, config):
+        model = self.make_model(config)
+        before = {n: p.data_ptr() for n, p in model.named_parameters()}
+        self.make_decode(config, model)
+        after = {n: p.data_ptr() for n, p in model.named_parameters()}
+        assert before == after

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""The reference kernel: a ``DecodeImpl`` over the layers it replaces."""
+
+from dataclasses import replace
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config.compilation import CUDAGraphMode
+from vllm.forward_context import get_forward_context
+from vllm.models.common.specialized_decode.spec import DecodeSpec, Step
+
+CACHE_DTYPE = torch.bfloat16
+CACHE_NDIM = 4
+
+
+class ReferenceLayer(torch.nn.Module):
+    """A decoder layer the reference kernel can replace: one weight, one
+    attention layer name, and ``dense`` for the layers a spec skips."""
+
+    def __init__(self, index: int, hidden: int, dense: bool = False):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.index = index
+        self.dense = dense
+        self.attn_name = f"layers.{index}.attn"
+        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.ones(hidden) * index)
+
+    def forward(self, positions: torch.Tensor, hidden: torch.Tensor):
+        return hidden + self.weight
+
+
+class ReferenceModel(torch.nn.Module):
+    """A model shaped like the layer loop a kernel hooks into."""
+
+    def __init__(self, layers: int = 4, hidden: int = 8):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.config = SimpleNamespace(num_hidden_layers=layers, hidden_size=hidden)
+        self.layers = torch.nn.ModuleList(
+            [ReferenceLayer(i, hidden, dense=i == 0) for i in range(layers)]
+        )
+        self.start_layer = 0
+        self.end_layer = layers
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor | None,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        intermediate_tensors=None,
+        inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        hidden = inputs_embeds
+        for layer in self.layers:
+            hidden = layer(positions, hidden)
+        return hidden
+
+
+class ReferenceKernel:
+    """The model's decode in one launch: the work of every layer it replaces,
+    off views of the model's weights, with the dense layers left to vLLM."""
+
+    def __init__(self, vllm_config, model: ReferenceModel, widths: tuple[int, ...]):
+        self.model = model
+        self.widths = widths
+        served = [
+            model.layers[i]
+            for i in range(model.start_layer, model.end_layer)
+            if not model.layers[i].dense
+        ]
+        self.weights = {layer.index: layer.weight.data for layer in served}
+        self.cache_layers = tuple(layer.attn_name for layer in served)
+        self.launched: list[int] = []
+        self.bound: dict[str, Any] = {}
+        self.compiled: set[Any] = set()
+
+    def run(self, step: Step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs):
+        self.launched.append(step.kernel_width)
+        hidden = inputs_embeds
+        for layer in self.model.layers:
+            weight = self.weights.get(layer.index)
+            if weight is None:
+                hidden = layer(step.positions, hidden)
+            else:
+                hidden = hidden + weight
+        return hidden
+
+    def bind_caches(self, caches) -> None:
+        self.bound = dict(caches)
+
+    def warmup_keys(self) -> list[Any]:
+        return [(i, w) for i in self.weights for w in self.widths]
+
+    def compile(self, key: Any) -> None:
+        self.compiled.add(key)
+
+
+def widths(vllm_config) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+    most = vllm_config.scheduler_config.max_num_seqs
+    return tuple(w for w in (1, 2, 4, 8) if w <= most)
+
+
+def refuse_config(vllm_config) -> list[str]:
+    reasons = []
+    if not widths(vllm_config):
+        reasons.append("max_num_seqs below the smallest width")
+    if vllm_config.model_config.dtype is not torch.bfloat16:
+        reasons.append(f"dtype {vllm_config.model_config.dtype}: needs bfloat16")
+    return reasons
+
+
+def refuse_model(model) -> list[str]:
+    return [] if isinstance(model, ReferenceModel) else ["not a ReferenceModel"]
+
+
+def skip_step(vllm_config, kernel: ReferenceKernel, width: int) -> str | None:
+    md = get_forward_context().attn_metadata
+    return "prefill" if md.get("prefill") else None
+
+
+def refuse_caches(vllm_config, kernel: ReferenceKernel, caches) -> list[str]:
+    reasons = []
+    for name, cache in caches.items():
+        if cache.dtype is not CACHE_DTYPE:
+            reasons.append(f"{name}: dtype {cache.dtype}, needs {CACHE_DTYPE}")
+        if cache.ndim != CACHE_NDIM:
+            reasons.append(f"{name}: {cache.ndim}d, needs {CACHE_NDIM}d")
+    return reasons
+
+
+def build(vllm_config, model, widths: tuple[int, ...]) -> ReferenceKernel:
+    return ReferenceKernel(vllm_config, model, widths)
+
+
+REFERENCE = DecodeSpec[ReferenceKernel](
+    name="reference",
+    supports=frozenset(),
+    widths=widths,
+    refuse_config=refuse_config,
+    refuse_model=refuse_model,
+    refuse_caches=refuse_caches,
+    skip_step=skip_step,
+    build=build,
+)
+
+REFERENCE_WIDE = replace(
+    REFERENCE,
+    name="reference-wide",
+    refuse_config=lambda c: (
+        refuse_config(c)
+        + (["needs max_num_seqs >= 8"] if c.scheduler_config.max_num_seqs < 8 else [])
+    ),
+)
+
+DECODE_SPECS = (REFERENCE_WIDE, REFERENCE)
+
+
+def make_config(**overrides) -> Any:
+    """A config shaped like the parts of ``VllmConfig`` the library reads.
+
+    Args:
+        **overrides: Top-level attributes to replace. Nested ones are set on
+            the returned object (``config.parallel_config.enable_eplb = True``).
+
+    """
+    config = SimpleNamespace(
+        kernel_config=SimpleNamespace(specialized_decode="monokernel"),
+        model_config=SimpleNamespace(dtype=torch.bfloat16, enable_sleep_mode=False),
+        scheduler_config=SimpleNamespace(max_num_seqs=4),
+        parallel_config=SimpleNamespace(
+            pipeline_parallel_size=1,
+            data_parallel_size=1,
+            enable_expert_parallel=False,
+            enable_eplb=False,
+            decode_context_parallel_size=1,
+            use_ubatching=False,
+            prefill_context_parallel_size=1,
+        ),
+        offload_config=SimpleNamespace(
+            uva=SimpleNamespace(cpu_offload_gb=0),
+            prefetch=SimpleNamespace(offload_group_size=0),
+        ),
+        aux_output_config=SimpleNamespace(enable_return_routed_experts=False),
+        compilation_config=SimpleNamespace(
+            cudagraph_mode=CUDAGraphMode.FULL,
+            cudagraph_capture_sizes=[1, 2, 3, 4, 16],
+            static_forward_context={},
+        ),
+        lora_config=None,
+        kv_transfer_config=None,
+        speculative_config=None,
+        weight_transfer_config=None,
+        use_v2_model_runner=True,
+    )
+    for key, value in overrides.items():
+        setattr(config, key, value)
+    return config
+
+
+def make_model(config, layers: int = 4) -> ReferenceModel:
+    """A loaded reference model, with its KV caches already in the config's
+    static forward context."""
+    model = ReferenceModel(layers=layers)
+    set_caches(config, model)
+    return model
+
+
+def set_caches(config, model, **kwargs) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Puts one cache a layer in the static forward context, and returns them."""
+    caches = {
+        layer.attn_name: make_cache(**kwargs)
+        for layer in model.layers
+        if not layer.dense
+    }
+    config.compilation_config.static_forward_context = {
+        name: SimpleNamespace(kv_cache=cache) for name, cache in caches.items()
+    }
+    return caches
+
+
+def make_cache(dtype=torch.bfloat16, ndim: int = 4) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.zeros((2,) + (1,) * (ndim - 1), dtype=dtype)

+
+def _norm() -> Any:

+def _moe(**overrides) -> Any:
+    experts = SimpleNamespace(
+        w13_weight=_bytes(4, HIDDEN),
+        w13_weight_scale=_bytes(4, 4),

+class _Layer(torch.nn.Module):

+        self.use_sequence_parallel = False
+        self.fuse_seam_norm = True

+        self.mhc_post = lambda x, residual, post, res: residual
+        for key, value in overrides.items():
+            setattr(self, key, value)
+        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(HIDDEN))
+        self.taken: list = []
+
+    def forward(self, x, positions, input_ids, *rest, decode_ffn=None):
+        self.taken.append(("layer", self.attn.layer_id, decode_ffn is not None))

+def _stream() -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:

+    return (
+        torch.zeros(1, HIDDEN),
+        torch.zeros(1, 4, HIDDEN),
+        torch.zeros(1, 4, 1),

+    def after_layer(

+DRAFT_LAYERS = 2
+DRAFT_EXPERTS = 128
+DRAFT_TOPK = 3
+DRAFT_TOKENS = 5

+class _DraftModel(torch.nn.Module):
+    """The DSpark draft head's backbone: its own layers, routing and stream."""
+
+    def __init__(self, config):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.config = config.model_config.hf_config
+        self.vllm_config = config
+        self.layers = torch.nn.ModuleList(
+            _Layer(
+                LAYERS + i,
+                attn=dict(compress_ratio=0),
+                ffn=dict(
+                    n_routed_experts=DRAFT_EXPERTS, n_activated_experts=DRAFT_TOPK
+                ),
+            )
+            for i in range(DRAFT_LAYERS)
+        )
+        self.hc_mult = 4
+
+    def prologue(self, input_ids, positions, inputs_embeds):
+        return inputs_embeds, input_ids, positions.shape[0]
+
+    def epilogue(self, hidden, *rest):
+        return hidden
+
+
+def make_draft_config(**overrides) -> Any:
+    config = make_config(**overrides)
+    config.speculative_config = SimpleNamespace(
+        num_speculative_tokens=DRAFT_TOKENS, method="dspark"
+    )
+    hf = config.model_config.hf_config
+    hf.sliding_window = sd.SWA_WIDTH
+    hf.dspark_n_routed_experts = DRAFT_EXPERTS
+    hf.dspark_num_experts_per_tok = DRAFT_TOPK
+    return config
+
+
+def _build_draft(monkeypatch, config=None, model=None):
+    _gpu(monkeypatch)
+    config = config or make_draft_config()
+    model = model if model is not None else _DraftModel(config)
+    sfc = config.compilation_config.static_forward_context
+    for layer in model.layers:
+        layer.attn.swa_cache_layer.kv_cache = make_cache()
+        sfc[layer.attn.swa_cache_layer.prefix] = layer.attn.swa_cache_layer
+    spec = select_decode_spec(config, sd.DRAFT_DECODE_SPEC)
+    return SpecializedDecode(model, config, spec), model
+
+
+def _draft_metadata(model, **overrides) -> dict:
+    width = sd.draft_swa_width(model.vllm_config)
+    fields = dict(
+        decode_swa_width=width,
+        decode_swa_indices=torch.zeros(8, 1, width, dtype=torch.int32),
+    )
+    return {
+        layer.attn.swa_cache_layer.prefix: _swa(**(fields | overrides))
+        for layer in model.layers
+    }

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Dispatcher for specialized decoder kernels.
+
+Performs validation, jit registration, planning, and dispatching of specialized decode
+kernels for a model based on a given specification.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Generic
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config.compilation import CUDAGraphMode
+from vllm.forward_context import get_forward_context, is_forward_context_available
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.warmup.jit_warmup import VllmJitKernel
+from vllm.models.common.specialized_decode.guards import (
+    _refuse_model,
+    tp_agree,
+    tp_group,
+)
+from vllm.models.common.specialized_decode.spec import (
+    DecodeSpec,
+    DecodeUnsupported,
+    DecodeWarmable,
+    KernelT,
+    Step,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+class DecodeWarmup(VllmJitKernel["DecodeWarmup.CompileKey"]):
+    """A spec's kernel builds as vLLM JIT warm-up keys."""
+
+    @dataclass(frozen=True)
+    class CompileKey:
+        spec: str
+        build: Any
+
+    def __init__(self, spec: str, kernel: DecodeWarmable):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.spec = spec
+        self.kernel = kernel
+
+    def get_warmup_keys(self) -> list["DecodeWarmup.CompileKey"]:
+        return [self.CompileKey(self.spec, b) for b in self.kernel.warmup_keys()]
+
+    def compile(self, compile_key: "DecodeWarmup.CompileKey") -> None:
+        self.kernel.compile(compile_key.build)
+        self._compiled_cache[compile_key] = True
+
+
+class SpecializedDecode(Generic[KernelT]):
+    """A model's specialized decode on this rank.
+
+    It reads the spec and builds the kernel, registers it for warm-up if it
+    compiles from keys, checks the caches whenever the runner binds them, and
+    decides each step
+    between the kernel and vLLM's own forward. The kernel it builds is held in
+    the ``kernel`` attribute.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, model, vllm_config: "VllmConfig", spec: DecodeSpec[KernelT]):
+        """Builds this rank's kernel.
+
+        Args:
+            model: The loaded model, in ``process_weights_after_loading``.
+            vllm_config: The engine's config.
+            spec: The spec to build and run.
+
+        """
+        self.spec = spec
+        reasons = _refuse_model(spec, model)
+        agreed = tp_agree(not reasons, tp_group()[2])
+        refused = f"Specialized decode {spec.name} refused for the loaded model"
+        if reasons:
+            raise DecodeUnsupported(f"{refused}: " + "; ".join(reasons))
+        if not agreed:
+            raise DecodeUnsupported(f"{refused}: another TP rank refused")
+        self.vllm_config = vllm_config
+        self.widths = tuple(sorted(spec.widths(vllm_config)))
+        self._bound = False
+        self.kernel: KernelT = spec.build(vllm_config, model, self.widths)
+        kernel = self.kernel
+        if isinstance(kernel, DecodeWarmable) and kernel.warmup_keys():
+            DecodeWarmup(spec.name, kernel).register_warmup()
+        logger.info("Specialized decode %s: widths %s", spec.name, list(self.widths))
+
+    def bind_caches(self) -> None:
+        """Validate and bind caches to the kernel.
+
+        The underlying kernel only ever sees caches this spec has accepted.
+        """
+        sfc = self.vllm_config.compilation_config.static_forward_context
+        caches = {n: sfc[n].kv_cache for n in self.kernel.cache_layers}
+        reasons = self.spec.refuse_caches(self.vllm_config, self.kernel, caches)
+        if reasons:
+            raise DecodeUnsupported(
+                f"Specialized decode {self.spec.name} caches: " + "; ".join(reasons)
+            )
+        self.kernel.bind_caches(caches)
+        self._bound = True
+
+    def _kernel_width(self, width: int) -> int | None:
+        """The width the kernel launches at for a step of ``width`` rows, or
+        None when the spec serves no width for it."""
+        if self.spec.pad_steps:
+            return next((w for w in self.widths if w >= width), None)
+        return width if width in self.widths else None
+
+    def plan(self, positions: torch.Tensor, intermediate_tensors=None) -> Step | None:
+        """This step's plan, or None to run the model's own forward instead.
+
+        A step can fall back to running the model's own forward when the kernel cannot
+        serve it, as described by the spec.
+        """
+        width = positions.size(-1)
+        kernel_width = self._kernel_width(width)
+        why: str | None
+        if intermediate_tensors is not None:
+            why = "pipeline stage input"
+        elif kernel_width is None:
+            why = "width"
+        elif not is_forward_context_available():
+            why = "no forward context"
+        elif get_forward_context().cudagraph_runtime_mode == CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE:
+            why = "piecewise"
+        elif not self._bound:
+            why = "caches not bound"
+        else:
+            why = self.spec.skip_step(self.vllm_config, self.kernel, kernel_width)
+        if why is not None:
+            logger.info_once(
+                "Specialized decode %s: step on vLLM's path (%s)", self.spec.name, why
+            )
+            return None
+        assert kernel_width is not None
+        return Step(width=width, kernel_width=kernel_width, positions=positions)
+
+    def run(self, step: Step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs) -> Any:
+        """Run the specialized kernel, returning what the model's own forward would
+        have returned."""
+        return self.kernel.run(step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Common validation logic for specialized decode kernels."""
+
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+from vllm.config.compilation import CUDAGraphMode
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.models.common.specialized_decode.spec import (
+    DecodeSpec,
+    DecodeUnsupported,
+    Feature,
+    KernelT,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+_FULL_MODES = (
+    CUDAGraphMode.NONE,
+    CUDAGraphMode.FULL,
+    CUDAGraphMode.FULL_DECODE_ONLY,
+    CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE,
+)
+
+
+def tp_group() -> tuple[int, int, object | None]:
+    """This rank's (rank, world size, CPU group) in the TP group, and
+    (0, 1, None) before distributed is initialized."""
+    if not dist.is_available() or not dist.is_initialized():
+        return 0, 1, None
+    from vllm.distributed import get_tp_group
+
+    tp = get_tp_group()
+    return tp.rank_in_group, tp.world_size, tp.cpu_group
+
+
+def tp_agree(ok: bool, group) -> bool:
+    """Agree on a boolean across the TP group.
+
+    Args:
+        ok: This rank's local verdict.
+        group: The TP group's CPU (gloo) process group, or None for one rank.
+
+    """
+    if group is None:
+        return ok
+    flag = torch.tensor([int(ok)], dtype=torch.int32)
+    dist.all_reduce(flag, op=dist.ReduceOp.MIN, group=group)
+    return bool(flag.item())
+
+
+def _enabled(vllm_config: "VllmConfig") -> bool:
+    """Whether the engine is configured to run specialized decode."""
+    return bool(vllm_config.kernel_config.specialized_decode)
+
+
+def _features_in_use(vllm_config: "VllmConfig") -> set[Feature]:
+    """Features in use by this config."""
+    pc = vllm_config.parallel_config
+    oc = vllm_config.offload_config
+    on = {
+        Feature.PIPELINE_PARALLEL: pc.pipeline_parallel_size > 1,
+        Feature.DATA_PARALLEL: pc.data_parallel_size > 1,
+        Feature.EXPERT_PARALLEL: pc.enable_expert_parallel,
+        Feature.EPLB: pc.enable_eplb,
+        Feature.DECODE_CONTEXT_PARALLEL: pc.decode_context_parallel_size > 1,
+        Feature.UBATCHING: pc.use_ubatching,
+        Feature.PREFILL_CONTEXT_PARALLEL: pc.prefill_context_parallel_size > 1,
+        Feature.LORA: vllm_config.lora_config is not None,
+        Feature.KV_CONNECTOR: vllm_config.kv_transfer_config is not None,
+        Feature.ROUTED_EXPERT_CAPTURE: (
+            vllm_config.aux_output_config.enable_return_routed_experts
+        ),
+        Feature.SPECULATIVE_DECODING: vllm_config.speculative_config is not None,
+        Feature.SLEEP_MODE: vllm_config.model_config.enable_sleep_mode,
+        Feature.CPU_WEIGHT_OFFLOAD: (
+            oc.uva.cpu_offload_gb > 0 or oc.prefetch.offload_group_size > 0
+        ),
+        Feature.WEIGHT_UPDATES: vllm_config.weight_transfer_config is not None,
+    }
+    return {f for f, used in on.items() if used}
+
+
+def _refuse_config(spec: DecodeSpec[Any], vllm_config: "VllmConfig") -> list[str]:
+    """The reasons the config cannot run the specialized decode kernel, if any."""
+    reasons = [
+        f"{f.value} is not supported"
+        for f in sorted(_features_in_use(vllm_config) - spec.supports)
+    ]
+    if not vllm_config.use_v2_model_runner:
+        reasons.append("needs Model Runner V2")
+    mode = vllm_config.compilation_config.cudagraph_mode
+    if mode is not None and mode not in _FULL_MODES:
+        reasons.append(f"CUDA graph mode {mode.name}: decode needs FULL graphs")
+    return reasons + list(spec.refuse_config(vllm_config))
+
+
+def _refuse_model(spec: DecodeSpec[Any], model) -> list[str]:
+    """The reasons the mode cannot run the specialized decode kernel, if any."""
+    from vllm.compilation.wrapper import TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper
+
+    reasons = []
+    if isinstance(model, TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper):
+        reasons.append(
+            "model is torch.compile'd: specialized decode replaces the layer loop, "
+            "so the model must not carry @support_torch_compile"
+        )
+    return reasons + list(spec.refuse_model(model))
+
+
+def _select_spec(
+    specs: Sequence[DecodeSpec[Any]], vllm_config: "VllmConfig"
+) -> tuple[DecodeSpec[Any] | None, dict[str, list[str]]]:
+    """Get the first compatible spec."""
+    refusals: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+    for spec in specs:
+        reasons = _refuse_config(spec, vllm_config)
+        if not reasons:
+            return spec, refusals
+        refusals[spec.name] = reasons
+    return None, refusals
+
+
+def _set_capture_sizes(spec: DecodeSpec[Any], vllm_config: "VllmConfig") -> None:
+    """Amend the capture sizes with the supported widths, so that no step is
+    refused for its width alone."""
+    cc = vllm_config.compilation_config
+    widths = spec.widths(vllm_config)
+    sizes = cc.cudagraph_capture_sizes or []
+    new = sorted(set(widths) | {s for s in sizes if s > max(widths)})
+    if new != sorted(sizes):
+        logger.info(
+            "Specialized decode %s: CUDA graph capture sizes %s", spec.name, new
+        )
+        cc.cudagraph_capture_sizes = new
+
+
+def select_decode_spec(
+    vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+    specs: DecodeSpec[KernelT] | Sequence[DecodeSpec[KernelT]],
+) -> DecodeSpec[KernelT] | None:
+    """Select the first compatible spec and, unless it declines them, set the
+    capture sizes to its widths.
+
+    Args:
+        vllm_config: The engine's config, before the weights are loaded.
+        specs: The model's variants, in the order they are preferred.
+
+    """
+    if not _enabled(vllm_config):
+        return None
+    ordered = (specs,) if isinstance(specs, DecodeSpec) else tuple(specs)
+    spec, refusals = _select_spec(ordered, vllm_config)
+    if spec is None:
+        raise DecodeUnsupported(
+            "Specialized decode refused: "
+            + "; ".join(f"{n}: {', '.join(rs)}" for n, rs in refusals.items())
+        )
+    if spec.set_capture_sizes:
+        _set_capture_sizes(spec, vllm_config)
+    if vllm_config.compilation_config.cudagraph_mode == CUDAGraphMode.NONE:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Specialized decode %s under eager mode: for debugging only, serve "
+            "with FULL CUDA graphs",
+            spec.name,
+        )
+    return spec

+from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from enum import Enum
+from typing import (
+    TYPE_CHECKING,
+    Any,

+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:

+
+
+class Feature(str, Enum):
+    """Features a specialized decode kernel may require."""
+
+    PIPELINE_PARALLEL = "pipeline_parallel"
+    DATA_PARALLEL = "data_parallel"
+    EXPERT_PARALLEL = "expert_parallel"
+    EPLB = "eplb"
+    DECODE_CONTEXT_PARALLEL = "decode_context_parallel"
+    UBATCHING = "ubatching"
+    PREFILL_CONTEXT_PARALLEL = "prefill_context_parallel"
+    LORA = "lora"
+    KV_CONNECTOR = "kv_connector"
+    ROUTED_EXPERT_CAPTURE = "routed_expert_capture"
+    SPECULATIVE_DECODING = "speculative_decoding"
+    SLEEP_MODE = "sleep_mode"
+    CPU_WEIGHT_OFFLOAD = "cpu_weight_offload"
+    WEIGHT_UPDATES = "weight_updates"
+
+
+class DecodeUnsupported(Exception):
+    """The configuration or the loaded model is outside what a spec serves."""
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Step:
+    """One decode step the kernel takes, as ``SpecializedDecode.plan`` decided it."""
+
+    width: int
+    """The step's rows, as the model's forward was handed them."""
+
+    kernel_width: int
+    """The width the kernel launches at, one of the widths the spec serves.
+
+    Equal to ``width``, unless the spec pads a short step up to the next width
+    it was built for, in which case it is the larger of the two and the kernel
+    owns the padding.
+    """
+
+    positions: "torch.Tensor"
+    """The step's positions, as the model's forward was handed them."""
+
+
+class DecodeImpl(Protocol):
+    """A specialized decode kernel, substituting a model's forward.
+
+    The implementation owns its own layer loop, so the library has no opinion
+    about layers: it may replace one layer, two, or the whole backbone.
+    """
+
+    cache_layers: tuple[str, ...]
+    """Attention layers whose caches ``DecodeSpec.refuse_caches`` checks."""
+
+    def run(self, step: Step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs) -> Any:
+        """Takes and returns what the model's own forward does."""
+        ...
+
+    def bind_caches(self, caches: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
+        """Bind the KV caches the kernel will read."""
+        ...
+
+
+@runtime_checkable
+class DecodeWarmable(Protocol):
+    """A kernel whose launches compile from keys, registered for vLLM's JIT
+    warm-up.
+
+    SpecializedDecodes created inside process_weights_after_loading can implement
+    this for automatic warm-up of their kernels, so that the first decode step does not
+    pay the compilation cost.
+    """
+
+    def warmup_keys(self) -> list[Any]:
+        """Build keys of this kernel's launches."""
+        ...
+
+    def compile(self, key: Any) -> None:
+        """Compiles one of ``warmup_keys`` without launching it."""
+        ...
+
+
+KernelT = TypeVar("KernelT", bound=DecodeImpl)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class DecodeSpec(Generic[KernelT]):
+    """Definition of when specialized decode can run, and how to build its
+    implementation.
+
+    Attributes:
+        name: Log and metric name.
+        supports: Features this spec serves. Default deny: a feature in use
+            that is absent from it refuses the deployment.
+        widths: The rows a launch serves, from the engine's config.
+        refuse_config: Conditions under which the specialized decode kernel cannot run,
+            based on the config.
+        refuse_model: Conditions under which the specialized decode kernel cannot run,
+            based on the model.
+        refuse_caches: Conditions under which the specialized decode kernel cannot run,
+            based on the cache.
+        skip_step: Whether to run the specialized decode kernel for this forward call,
+            or to fall back to the model's own forward. Takes the step's
+            ``kernel_width``.
+        build: This rank's kernel.
+        pad_steps: Whether a step of fewer rows than a served width runs on the
+            next width up, the kernel padding it. Default deny: a step whose
+            rows are not themselves a served width falls back.
+        set_capture_sizes: Whether to make the served widths the CUDA graph
+            capture sizes, so that no step is refused for its width alone. Turn
+            it off for a spec that pads, which serves the engine's own capture
+            sizes as they are.
+
+    """
+
+    name: str
+    supports: frozenset[Feature]
+    widths: Callable[["VllmConfig"], tuple[int, ...]]
+    refuse_config: Callable[["VllmConfig"], list[str]]
+    refuse_model: Callable[[Any], list[str]]
+    refuse_caches: Callable[["VllmConfig", KernelT, Mapping[str, Any]], list[str]]
+    skip_step: Callable[["VllmConfig", KernelT, int], str | None]
+    build: Callable[["VllmConfig", Any, tuple[int, ...]], KernelT]
+    pad_steps: bool = False
+    set_capture_sizes: bool = True

-def _keep_copies(layer, copies: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]) -> None:

-    weights (``reload_weights``, or a weight update in RL) runs

-    """gfx942: the kernels read their own copies of the layer's weights. Make
-    them when vLLM processes the weights at load, so that they count as model
-    memory when vLLM sizes the KV cache. Copies made at the first decode step
-    would count only when that step is also the CUDA graph memory profile, so
-    with that profile off or with ``enforce_eager`` they would not count. A
-    layer that takes only the FFN launch needs no attention copies."""

-    attn = layer.attn

+"""DeepSeek-V4.1's decode kernels: one launch a layer over the stock backbone,
+and the same over the DSpark draft head's layers."""

+from vllm.models.common.specialized_decode.spec import Step

+    DRAFT_UG_GROUPS,
+    EXPERTS,
+    MAX_ROWS,
+    RECORD,
+    SWA_WIDTH,
+    TOPK,
+    UG_GROUPS,
+    draft_routing,
+    draft_swa_width,
+    on_gfx942,
+)

+def _record_view(kv: torch.Tensor, block: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """A layer's fp8_ds_mla cache as [blocks, block, RECORD] bytes (a block's
+    data rows, then its scale words: the kernels index both from it).
+
+    A block's stride has to span every record in it, or the next block starts
+    inside this one. ``_refuse_caches`` screens this at startup from the KV
+    cache spec; here the step's own block size settles it.
+    """
+    kv = kv if kv.dtype == torch.uint8 else kv.view(torch.uint8)
+    assert kv.stride(0) >= block * RECORD, (tuple(kv.shape), kv.stride(), block)
+    return torch.as_strided(kv, (kv.shape[0], block, RECORD), (kv.stride(0), RECORD, 1))
+
+
+def _select(
+    layer: "DeepseekV4DecoderLayer",
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    normed: torch.Tensor,
+    qr: torch.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    """An index source's compressor and top-k selection, from K1's normed input
+    and bf16 qr: ``_forward_csa2_full`` / ``_forward_csa2_reindex`` and the
+    indexer op, serial."""
+    attn = layer.attn
+    comp, indexer = attn.compressor, attn.indexer
+    assert indexer is not None
+    if comp is not None:
+        kv_score = torch.mm(
+            normed, comp.fused_wkv_wgate.weight.T, out_dtype=torch.float32
+        )
+        latent = comp(kv_score, positions)
+        comp.insert_cache(latent, positions, attn.rotary_emb)
+        indexer._produce_k(latent, positions, attn.indexer_rotary_emb)
+    weights, _ = indexer.weights_proj(normed)
+    q, q_scale, weights = indexer.forward_q(
+        qr, None, weights, positions, attn.indexer_rotary_emb
+    )
+    assert weights is not None
+    indexer.indexer_op(
+        normed, (q, q_scale) if q_scale is not None else q, None, weights
+    )
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class LayerPlan:
+    """One decoder layer's launch, settled at load.
+
+    An ``ffn_only`` layer keeps vLLM's attention and its launch takes wo_b's
+    unreduced output, so its weights are all it has; the rest is what a
+    whole-layer launch reads off the layer.
+    """
+
+    layer: "DeepseekV4DecoderLayer"
+    weights: Any
+    ffn_only: bool
+    ratio: int = 0
+    index: bool = False
+    swa_key: str | None = None
+    comp_key: str | None = None
+    folds: tuple[bool, ...] = ()
+
+
+class LayerLaunches:
+    """The launches of one stack of DSv4.1 decoder layers: the backbone's, or
+    the DSpark draft's, which has its own routing, SWA rows and runner.
+
+    A subclass owns the layer loop in ``run``; everything the launches need is
+    settled here, at load.
+    """
+
+    draft = False
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        vllm_config,
+        model,
+        widths: tuple[int, ...],
+        experts: int,
+        topk: int,
+        ug_groups: int,
+        swa_width: int,
+    ):
+        from vllm.models.common.specialized_decode.guards import tp_group
+        from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.runner import (
+            MAX_TOKENS,
+            DSV41MonoLayer,
+        )
+
+        assert MAX_TOKENS >= MAX_ROWS, MAX_TOKENS
+        rank, world, cpu_group = tp_group()
+        device = next(model.parameters()).device
+        self.model = model
+        self.experts, self.topk, self.swa_width = experts, topk, swa_width
+        self.runner = DSV41MonoLayer(
+            world,
+            rank,
+            cpu_group,
+            device,
+            experts=experts,
+            topk=topk,
+            ug_groups=ug_groups,
+            swa_width=swa_width,
+        )
+        self.embed_layer = getattr(model, "start_layer", 0)
+        # A decode step is never trimmed, so ``run`` owns every layer, the ones
+        # past the replay cut included.
+        self.layer_end = getattr(model, "end_layer", len(model.layers))
+        self.widths = widths
+        self.swa_keys: list[str] = []
+        self.comp_keys: list[str] = []
+        self.plans: dict[int, LayerPlan] = {}
+        self.block_records: dict[str, int] = {}
+
+        tp_size = vllm_config.parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size
+        block_size = vllm_config.cache_config.block_size
+        for idx in range(self.embed_layer, self.layer_end):
+            layer = model.layers[idx]
+            plan = self._plan_layer(layer, tp_size, first=idx == self.embed_layer)
+            if plan is None:
+                continue
+            self.plans[layer.attn.layer_id] = plan
+            if plan.ffn_only:
+                continue
+            for key, keys, records in (
+                (plan.swa_key, self.swa_keys, layer.attn.swa_cache_layer.block_size),
+                (plan.comp_key, self.comp_keys, block_size // (plan.ratio or 1)),
+            ):
+                if key is None:
+                    continue
+                if key not in keys:
+                    keys.append(key)
+                self.block_records[key] = max(self.block_records.get(key, 0), records)
+        self.cache_layers = tuple(sorted(set(self.swa_keys) | set(self.comp_keys)))
+
+    def _plan_layer(self, layer, tp_size: int, first: bool) -> LayerPlan | None:
+        """Info needed to run the specialized decode kernel for this layer."""
+        attn = layer.attn
+        why = _skip_layer(layer, self.experts, self.topk, tp_size)
+        if why is not None:
+            logger.info_once(
+                "DSv4.1 specialized decode: layer %d on vLLM's path (%s)",
+                attn.layer_id,
+                why,
+            )
+            return None
+        if self.draft and on_gfx942():
+            # On gfx942 the draft layers take the FFN launch after vLLM's
+            # attention. vLLM's draft MoE multiplies bf16 activations with the
+            # FP4 experts, and the FFN launch quantizes them to MXFP8 as it does
+            # for the target. That changes only how many drafts the target
+            # accepts, not the target's output.
+            logger.info_once(
+                "DSv4.1 specialized decode: the FFN launch for the draft layers "
+                "(%d / %d routing)",
+                self.experts,
+                self.topk,
+            )
+            return self._ffn_plan(layer, tp_size)
+        why = _ffn_only(layer)
+        if why is None and self.draft and (attn.compress_ratio or attn.indexer):
+            why = "compressed keys"
+        if why is not None and self.draft:
+            # The draft has no FFN launch: its layers run whole or not at all.
+            logger.info_once(
+                "DSv4.1 specialized decode: the draft layers on vLLM's path (%s)", why
+            )
+            return None
+        if why is not None:
+            logger.info_once(
+                "DSv4.1 specialized decode: the FFN launch for layers with %s", why
+            )
+            return self._ffn_plan(layer, tp_size)
+        weights = _weights(layer, False, tp_size, self.experts)
+        # gfx942: the entry seam of a whole first layer projects the expanded
+        # residual with the unfolded hc_attn_fn, as K1 does, and not the
+        # embedding with the folded copy, which has no AITER kernel there.
+        layer.unfolded_entry = on_gfx942()
+        comp_key = attn.compressed_cache_prefix if attn.compress_ratio else None

+        # residual arrives settled: the embedding, or after the Engram write.
+        settled = first or layer.engram is not None
+        return LayerPlan(
+            layer,
+            weights,
+            ffn_only=False,
+            ratio=attn.compress_ratio,
+            index=attn.indexer is not None,
+            swa_key=attn.swa_cache_layer.prefix,
+            comp_key=comp_key,
+            folds=(True, False) if settled else (True,),
+        )
+
+    def _ffn_plan(self, layer, tp_size: int) -> LayerPlan:
+        # A decode step hands wo_b's TP partial to the FFN launch; the layer
+        # reduces it on the steps that keep vLLM's path.
+        layer.attn.wo_b.reduce_results = False
+        return LayerPlan(
+            layer, _weights(layer, True, tp_size, self.experts), ffn_only=True
+        )
+
+    def bind_caches(self, caches: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
+        """Nothing to take: a launch reads the cache off its attention layer."""

+    def warmup_keys(self) -> list[Any]:
+        keys: dict[Any, None] = {}
+        for plan in self.plans.values():
+            for width in self.widths:
+                if plan.ffn_only:
+                    keys[width, "ffn", self.experts, self.topk] = None
+                else:
+                    for fold in plan.folds:
+                        keys[width, plan.ratio, fold, plan.index] = None

+
+    def compile(self, key: Any) -> None:
+        self.runner.scratch(key[0])
+        if key[1] == "ffn":
+            self.runner.ffn_kernel(key[0], key[2], key[3])
+        else:
+            width, ratio, fold, index = key
+            self.runner.kernels(width, ratio, fold=fold, index=index)
+

+        res_mix: torch.Tensor | None,
+        pre_mix: torch.Tensor | None,

+        # hc copies ([rows, hc, dim]), the backbone's the 2-D embedding.
